title: The influence of high-frequency stimlution on the symptoms of complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS)
summary:
The study examines the impact of the therapy with TipStim® to patients with CRPS (complex regional pain syndrome) affecting the hand. The probands receive directly or after a non-effective four-week long sham-stimulation a three-month long therapy with the TipStim®. The TipStim® is a glove, which is working with electric stimulation and can possibly improve the sensorimotor coupling and sensory and motor function in patients with CRPS. The probands perform the therapy at home for one hour every day.
Three examinations are performed at the UKSH (university medical centre Schleswig- Holstein). The first examination takes place at the beginning of the study. The second examination is only for probands who are receiving the sham-stimulation. Both groups receive a final examination after three months of therapy with TipStim®.
Each examination includes a fMRT, functional tests, questionnaires, clinical examination and quantitative sensory testing. Afterwards the results will be analysed regarding the impact of the TipStim®.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Budapest criteria fulfilled, no differential diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
pregnancy or nursing
severe infections
cancer
polyneuropathie or other diseases with influence on the somatosensory system (relative ec)
cognitive deficits
not fluent in German
contraindications for MRI
